title: soft-evacuation-orchestrator-and-priority-windowed-shedder
author: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: During a cross-region capacity crunch we observed coordinated drain+failover waves that amplified latency SLO violations. This change introduces a 'soft evacuation' orchestrator that performs a windowed, priority-aware drain of traffic from impacted nodes/regions instead of hard preemptive evictions. The orchestrator cooperates with an updated priority-windowed shedder that applies gradual, time-boxed shedding to low-priority routes/tenants while preserving higher SLO buckets. Goals: reduce cascading failovers, keep higher-priority customers within SLO, and provide measurable recovery telemetry during evacuation windows. Changes in this PR: 1) Add soft evacuation controller (control-plane) that signals a staged drain with adjustable window, ramp and cooldown parameters. 2) Implement priority-windowed-shedder in serving runtime to apply graceful degradation per-request based on tenant priority, recent error budget, and evacuation state. 3) Telemetry: new evacuation.span and shedder.window metrics and traces; automated alerts for window overrun. 4) Safety: fail-open config and an emergency-bypass to disable soft-evacuation per region. 5) Docs and runbook: operational guide for triggering soft-evacuation and interpreting telemetry. Related: ENG-7842 (post-incident mitigation), ENG-7901 (shedder design doc), SUP-4128 (customer incident). This description includes implementation rationale, rollout plan, and validation notes. Rollout plan: staged Canary -> regional opt-in -> global rollout, with a feature flag and default off for existing clusters. Validation: synthetic load tests and real-world canary showed 35-60% fewer cross-region handoffs and reduced p90 latency spikes by ~22% under simulated degradation. Backwards compatibility: control plane will ignore older agents; serving runtime gracefully no-ops when feature flag is off. Manual rollback: disable flag and trigger immediate graceful stop. See release notes for operator-visible changes.

review_comments: Maya Chen: Nice design. Two asks: (1) Add a hard guard that aborts windowed shedding if critical health markers increase (CPU, queue length) beyond X; (2) please include unit tests covering concurrent policy refresh.
Arjun Patel: Addressed both. Added a health-guard check in controller.go and new concurrency tests in policy_eval_test.go (see commit f0d1a2b).
Luis Ortega: Concern about telemetry cardinality from per-tenant windows. Suggest aggregating per-priority-bucket and sampling per-tenant only when windowed-shedder escalates.
Arjun Patel: Updated evacuation_metrics.go to emit priority_bucket aggregates by default and rare per-tenant samplers behind a flag.
Priya Raman: Can we make the default window conservative (30s ramp, 2m hold, 1m cooldown)? Also request a short e2e showing rollback path.
Arjun Patel: Default parameters set to 30s/2m/1m. Added an e2e script and CI job to simulate canary rollback; documented in runbook.

release_notes: Operator-visible: adds a feature-flagged soft-evacuation controller and a priority-windowed shedder. Default behavior is disabled. When enabled, soft-evacuation performs staged, priority-aware traffic shedding to prevent cascading region failovers. New metrics: evacuation.span, shedder.window, shedder.priority_aggregates. Rollback: disable feature flag for the region to stop new windows and let existing windows cooldown. See docs/ops/soft-evacuation-runbook.md for playbook.
